description: Prompts that read an AI system diagram (image, Mermaid, or SVG) and write a threat matrix plus a readable report. Track A walks Shostack's Four Questions; each step is filled with the previous step's JSON. STRIDE runs in auditable batches when a diagram exceeds one response. Track B, when selected after P-qa, writes layer, persona, and party before P-report finalizes the matrix. The export steps project that final matrix into markdown, JSON, CSV, and Mermaid.
lane: Track A inventories the diagram, records drawn controls and diagram-visible control gaps, elicits threats, classifies them, and chooses actions. P-stride repeats until its coverage object is complete. Optional Track B runs after P-qa and before P-report. P-report is the only author of report.markdown; the export steps emit projections of the final matrix.

scoring.aggregation_rule: Do not average automated and human scores into one number.
scoring.closure_rule: closure remains false until two reviewers per system complete the SME instruments and expert-corrected labels are scored.

citations.title: The Four Question Framework for Threat Modeling
citations.note: Do not rephrase the four questions.

citations.title: PHANTOM-B: A STRIDE Analog for LLMs
citations.note: Ask as questions on the LLM subset. The whitepaper excludes defenses; mitigations live in P-act.

citations.title: STRIDE
citations.note: Apply to the whole diagram, including non-LLM parts.

citations.title: Auspex: Building Threat Modeling Tradecraft into an Artificial Intelligence-based Copilot
citations.note: Two-stage chain, cumulative prompt fill, threat matrix, SME evaluation. The prompts here are rebuilt from the paper's published figures. JPMC's withheld tradecraft text is not in this pack.

citations.title: OAuth 2.0 Threat Model and Security Considerations
citations.note: Shape only: state attack assumptions and existing features before eliciting threats. Do not copy OAuth threats into an unrelated diagram.

shared_rules:
You are producing one step of a threat model for an AI system from a system representation (image, Mermaid, or SVG).

Rules:
- Use Shostack's Four Questions in this exact wording: What are we working on? What can go wrong? What are we going to do about it? Did we do a good job?
- Name the perspective: what we are working on right now, and which team view (application, platform, or model caller).
- Work only from the diagram and the prior chain output named in this prompt. Do not invent components, vendors, networks, or trust boundaries that are not drawn.
- If trust boundaries are missing from the diagram, set inventory.missing_trust_boundaries to true and record that as a finding. Do not invent boundaries silently.
- Every threat scenario must name a diagram_referent whose id exists in the inventory.
- Do not recite a generic catalog line (for example "LLMs can be prompt-injected") with no referent in this diagram.
- Do not use DREAD, OCTAVE, or attack trees as the primary method.
- PHANTOM-B is a set of questions for LLM and chatbot components. Do not force every STRIDE threat into a PHANTOM-B letter.
- Do not put mitigations, controls, or defenses in a PHANTOM-B elicitation step.
- Do not invent OWASP, ATLAS, or AI Exchange identifiers. Cite an id only if you are certain it exists; otherwise omit it.
- Use the output form named by the step. JSON steps output JSON only, with no markdown fences or commentary. Export steps output only the requested markdown, CSV, or Mermaid source.
- Once adversary.positions exists, every threat must set attacker_position to one of those ids.
- List an existing control only when a label, component, or flow on the diagram shows it.
- For mitigate or eliminate, action.validation is required: kind test, log, or fail_condition, plus detail a reviewer could run.
- Leave report.reviewer empty. A human fills it.

roles.label: Experienced threat modeler
roles.tradecraft: Role: experienced threat modeler. Enumerate concrete scenarios a builder could act on this sprint. Prefer data-flow and trust-boundary analysis over catalogs. When a STRIDE letter does not apply to an element, say so and give a reason.
notices_first: entry points, trust-boundary crossings, high-value stores, and controls whose shown coverage is uncertain
low-prerequisite attack paths available from an adversary position already recorded in the matrix
declines_to_opine: provider capacity, undocumented controls, or business impact that the diagram and prior matrix do not show
likelihood or residual-risk scores when the input supplies no evidence for them

roles.label: Application security
roles.tradecraft: Role: application security engineer. Focus on entry points, authn/authz, input mediation, session handling, and control points the application team can change. Keep a provider-owned infrastructure threat in scope only when the diagram shows it and the application team must demand evidence.
notices_first: public inputs that can bypass, disable, or choose whether a drawn filter runs
authorization decisions, session boundaries, parser transitions, and application-owned control points
declines_to_opine: provider DDoS capacity, datacenter controls, or model-training controls that are not shown
a provider-owned remediation when the application team can only require an attestation

roles.label: LLM caller
roles.tradecraft: Role: team that calls an LLM (hosted or local). Focus on prompt construction, tool and retrieval inputs, over-reliance, and what the model is allowed to decide. Do not assume you can retrain the base model.
notices_first: where untrusted content enters prompt assembly, retrieval, tools, memory, or model output handling
decisions or actions delegated to model output without a drawn approval or policy control
declines_to_opine: base-model retraining, provider internals, or training-data facts that are not shown
model intent, consciousness, guilt, or a provider guarantee not present in the diagram

four_questions.question: What are we going to do about it?
Did we do a good job?

phantom_b_questions.name: Prompt injection
phantom_b_questions.ask: How could someone prompt inject (direct, indirect, multi-stage) through this component?

phantom_b_questions.name: Hallucination
phantom_b_questions.ask: What if hallucinations exceed our hopes in this use of the component?

phantom_b_questions.name: Anthropomorphization
phantom_b_questions.ask: Are we anthropomorphizing this component (treating a token generator as if it had intent, guilt, or a model of user versus attacker)?

phantom_b_questions.name: Non-explainability
phantom_b_questions.ask: When must we explain or justify this component's output, and to whom? The model's own story is not an explanation.

phantom_b_questions.name: Training issues
phantom_b_questions.ask: What if training data is bad by accident or on purpose, and how does that show up at this call site?

phantom_b_questions.name: Over-reliance
phantom_b_questions.ask: What decisions does this LLM make, what control does it have, and does that expand the attack surface?

phantom_b_questions.name: Missing security engineering
phantom_b_questions.ask: Did we skip the rest of security engineering and the SDL around this LLM (authn, authz, logging, isolation, least privilege)?

phantom_b_questions.name: Biases
phantom_b_questions.ask: What biases does this model carry into this use case, and are they acceptable here?

prompts.title: Normalize representation
prompts.stop_condition: Inventory lists every visible component, actor, store, flow, and drawn trust boundary, with stable ids. representation.version and source_id are set or explicitly unknown. Distinct boxes remain distinct ids. replica_of is used only when the diagram explicitly shows one scaling group or managed pair. missing_trust_boundaries is true only when none are drawn.

prompts.title: Decompose diagram
prompts.stop_condition: Architecture description covers components, entry points, data flow, security boundaries, public vs private resources, external dependencies, and storage.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Shostack question: What are we working on?
Step: P-diag. Write a long-form architecture description of the system in the diagram.

Inventory from P-norm:
{{inventory}}

Original representation (kind={{representation_kind}}):
{{representation}}

Write architecture_description that covers:
- every component and how it relates to the others
- system entry points
- data flow
- security boundaries (drawn ones only)
- public vs private resources
- system availability or fault-tolerance properties only if the diagram shows them
- external dependencies
- storage and data security properties only if the diagram shows them

Return JSON:
{
  "architecture_description": "prose",
  "inventory": <echo the inventory; correct ids only if the diagram contradicts P-norm, and list corrections in a "corrections" array>
}

prompts.title: Application details
prompts.stop_condition: A concise statement of what the system does, who uses it, and what it must not do that is visible from the diagram.

prompts.title: Key features
prompts.stop_condition: Each key feature names something on the diagram that changes the threat surface (LLM call, retrieval, tools, identity, storage of prompts or documents).

prompts.title: In-scope components
prompts.stop_condition: Every inventory component is either in_scope or out_of_scope with a rationale tied to the named perspective. Each replica inheritance names a representative, replica, drawn evidence, paired component/flow/boundary ids, and a required divergence-gap scenario.

prompts.title: Solution description
prompts.stop_condition: solS explains how the architecture functions as one system and restates the structured DFD.

prompts.title: Attacker capabilities and claim boundary
prompts.stop_condition: adversary.assumptions is non-empty. Each drawn trust boundary or in-scope zone has a positions row. claim_boundary.does_not_claim and box are non-empty and tied to the diagram or the named perspective.

prompts.title: Existing security features
prompts.stop_condition: existing_controls lists only features shown on the diagram and records shown coverage without inference. control_absences records only that an expected control is not shown at a named inventory referent. Empty existing_controls is allowed only when none_drawn is true.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Shostack question: What are we working on?
Step: P-controls. Record security features already visible on the diagram and diagram-visible control gaps before writing threats. This is the RFC 6819 §3 shape: existing features first. Do not invent a control that is not drawn or named.

Solution description:
{{solution_description}}
Inventory:
{{inventory}}
Adversary:
{{adversary}}

Existing-control rules:
- Include authn, TLS, filters, isolation, logging, human approval, network policy, or identity providers only if a label, component, boundary, badge, or flow shows them.
- coverage_referents contains only inventory ids the diagram visibly connects, contains, or labels as protected.
- coverage_basis is connected, contained, label_only, badge_only, or unknown. A badge with no connecting line is badge_only and does not justify broader coverage.
- If no controls are drawn, return an empty existing_controls array and set none_drawn true.

Control-absence rules:
- A control_absence says only that the representation does not show the control at expected_referent. It does not claim the deployed system lacks it.
- expected_referent must be a component, store, flow, or trust-boundary id.
- Use a stable gap-ctl-* id so threat evidence_refs can cite the observation.

Return JSON:
{
  "existing_controls": [{
    "id": "ctl-...",
    "name": "",
    "diagram_referent": "inventory id where the control is drawn",
    "kind": "authn|tls|filter|isolation|logging|approval|network|identity|other",
    "coverage_referents": ["inventory ids visibly protected"],
    "coverage_basis": "connected|contained|label_only|badge_only|unknown"
  }],
  "control_absences": [{
    "id": "gap-ctl-...",
    "kind": "authn|tls|filter|isolation|logging|approval|network|identity|other",
    "expected_referent": "component, store, flow, or trust-boundary id",
    "observation": "what the diagram does not show and where"
  }],
  "none_drawn": false
}

prompts.title: Mark the LLM subset
prompts.stop_condition: llm_subset lists only chatbot, prompt-assembly, model-caller, or model-runtime nodes. llm_subset_empty equals whether the array is empty. An empty subset must carry a decision status and reason; do not report PHANTOM-B complete.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Shostack question: What are we working on?
Step: P-llm-cut. Mark which nodes receive PHANTOM-B. Per Shostack, PHANTOM-B applies to the front end and model runtime, not every box.

Solution description:
{{solution_description}}
Inventory:
{{inventory}}

Include a node if it: assembles or receives prompts, hosts a chatbot, runs an LLM, or calls an LLM endpoint.
Exclude a node if it only stores weights, serves as a generic database, or is a third-party hub that is not executing inference in this diagram.

Empty-subset rule:
- Set llm_subset_empty to true when llm_subset is empty.
- If inventory.llm_components or the diagram shows a prompt, chatbot, model caller, or model runtime, set status possible_miss and correct the subset before continuing.
- If no AI node is drawn, set status needs_operator_confirmation and stop. Ask whether to continue as a STRIDE-only model.
- After the operator confirms, rerun this step and set status continue_without_llm with the confirmation reason.
- A non-empty valid subset has status ready.

Return JSON:
{
  "llm_subset": ["component-id", "..."],
  "llm_subset_empty": false,
  "llm_subset_rationale": [{"id": "", "include": true, "reason": ""}],
  "llm_subset_decision": {
    "status": "ready|possible_miss|needs_operator_confirmation|continue_without_llm",
    "reason": ""
  }
}

prompts.title: STRIDE elicitation
prompts.stop_condition: Each required process and each crossing flow has six STRIDE consideration rows, directly or through documented replica inheritance. stride_coverage reports expected, considered, and remaining ids. Do not advance until stride_coverage.complete is true.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

{{role_guidance}}
Cyber role: {{cyber_role}}

Shostack question: What can go wrong?
Step: P-stride. Apply STRIDE to every in-scope process and every data flow that crosses a trust boundary. Run in auditable batches when the full set does not fit one response.

STRIDE letters: S spoofing, T tampering, R repudiation, I information disclosure, D denial of service, E elevation of privilege.

Batch rule:
- Maximum consideration rows in this reply: {{stride_budget}}. Process whole elements only, six rows per element.
- Determine expected_elements before writing rows: every in-scope process plus every crossing flow, minus replica ids whose coverage is explicitly inherited in replica_coverage.
- Count each required replica divergence row against the budget. rows_expected is six times the number of expected_elements plus one row per replica_coverage entry.
- Continue in inventory order after ids already present in prior_stride_considerations.
- Return stride_considerations as one cumulative array: prior rows followed by new rows, with no duplicate element_id and letter pair.
- If rows remain, set complete false and list remaining_elements. The operator reruns P-stride with this cumulative output as prior_stride_considerations.
- Never use the budget to reduce scope or silently omit an element.

Replica rule:
- Do not duplicate six rows for an inherited replica pair.
- Write one concrete configuration-divergence scenario for each replica_coverage row, normally under T tampering, using the replica id as diagram_referent.

Scenario rule:
- For each applicable letter, write one concrete scenario that can happen in this system.
- If a letter does not apply, record not_applicable with a reason. Do not skip a letter in silence.
- attacker_position must be an id from adversary.positions.
- evidence_refs may cite control_absences ids. A cited absence means the diagram does not show that control, not that the deployed system lacks it.

Solution description:
{{solution_description}}
Inventory:
{{inventory}}
In scope:
{{in_scope}}
Replica coverage:
{{replica_coverage}}
Adversary:
{{adversary}}
Existing controls:
{{existing_controls}}
Control absences:
{{control_absences}}
Claim boundary:
{{claim_boundary}}
Prior STRIDE considerations (empty on the first pass):
{{prior_stride_considerations}}

Return JSON:
{
  "stride_considerations": [
    {
      "element_id": "component or flow id",
      "letter": "S",
      "status": "scenario|not_applicable",
      "scenario": "concrete text or empty if not_applicable",
      "reason": "required when not_applicable",
      "diagram_referent": "element_id",
      "preconditions": "visible in the diagram",
      "evidence_refs": ["gap-ctl-id when applicable"],
      "attacker_position": "pos-id from adversary.positions",
      "asset": "what is harmed"
    }
  ],
  "stride_coverage": {
    "budget_rows": {{stride_budget}},
    "letters_per_element": 6,
    "expected_elements": ["ids"],
    "considered_elements": ["ids complete across all batches"],
    "remaining_elements": ["ids"],
    "rows_expected": 0,
    "rows_written_total": 0,
    "complete": false
  }
}

prompts.title: PHANTOM-B elicitation
prompts.stop_condition: Each non-empty llm_subset id has an answer to all eight PHANTOM-B questions. When llm_subset_empty is true after operator confirmation, phantom_considerations is empty and phantom_coverage.status is not_applicable. No mitigations.

prompts.title: Dedup and compose threat list
prompts.stop_condition: stride_coverage.complete is true before composition. TSS is numbered, duplicates are merged, each scenario has an inventory referent, evidence_refs are preserved, and each replica_coverage row names its divergence threat id.

prompts.title: CIA mapping
prompts.stop_condition: Every threat has a non-empty cia array of C, I, and/or A.

prompts.title: STRIDE mapping
prompts.stop_condition: Every threat has a non-empty stride array of S, T, R, I, D, and/or E.

prompts.title: PHANTOM-B mapping
prompts.stop_condition: PHANTOM-B letters appear only on threats whose diagram_referent is in llm_subset or whose source includes phantom-b. Other threats keep phantom_b as [].

prompts.title: Choose an action
prompts.stop_condition: Every threat has action.type in mitigate, eliminate, transfer, accept. Mitigate and eliminate name a control_point that is a component, store, flow, or trust-boundary id and a validation (test, log, or fail_condition).

prompts.title: Order threats for builder review
prompts.stop_condition: Every threat id appears exactly once in review_order. Ordering is explained from attacker_position and explicit preconditions. Threat ids and threats array order do not change. No likelihood, impact, or residual-risk claim is made.

prompts.title: Self-check
prompts.stop_condition: qa flags every failed check in gaps. Structured STRIDE and PHANTOM-B applicability, replica inheritance, control evidence, control-point ids, and action validation are checked. The full matrix is echoed. report_present stays false until P-report.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Shostack question: Did we do a good job?
Step: P-qa. Check the work before any human review.

Full threat matrix so far:
{{full_matrix}}

Checks:
1. inventory_components_in_solS: every inventory component id appears in solution_description.
2. boundary_crossings_covered: every crossing flow has a threat or an explicit replica_coverage inherited_element_pair whose representative is covered. A replica relation does not excuse an unmapped crossing.
3. llm_subset_empty: equals whether llm_subset is empty.
4. phantom_b_complete: null when llm_subset_empty is true after continue_without_llm; otherwise true only when every llm_subset id has all eight PHANTOM-B letters. Never use true for an empty subset.
5. stride_considered: stride_coverage.complete is true, remaining_elements is empty, and every expected element has six scenario or not_applicable rows, directly or by documented replica inheritance.
6. actions_complete: every threat has action.type in mitigate, eliminate, transfer, accept, and detail is not "pending P-act".
7. open_assumptions: list assumptions that are not on the diagram.
8. gaps: list failed checks in plain language.
9. adversary_stated: adversary.assumptions is non-empty and every in-scope trust boundary has a positions row, or a gap says which zone was skipped.
10. existing_controls_listed: existing_controls is present. Empty is allowed only when none_drawn is true. coverage_referents and coverage_basis do not claim more than the diagram shows.
11. control_absences_grounded: every control_absence says not shown, names an existing component, store, flow, or trust-boundary expected_referent, and avoids claiming deployed absence.
12. claim_boundary_stated: claim_boundary.does_not_claim and claim_boundary.box are non-empty.
13. actions_have_validation: every mitigate or eliminate action has validation.kind in test, log, fail_condition and non-empty detail.
14. control_points_bound: every mitigate or eliminate action.control_point is a component, data-store, data-flow, or trust-boundary id.
15. attacker_positions_bound: every threat.attacker_position is an id in adversary.positions.
16. evidence_refs_bound: every threat.evidence_refs value is a control_absences id.
17. replica_coverage_complete: every replica_coverage row has drawn evidence, valid inherited id pairs, and divergence_threat_id naming a threat on the replica.
18. review_order_complete: when review_order is present, every threat id appears exactly once and threat ids or array order did not change.

Also confirm every threats[].diagram_referent exists in inventory: component, external actor, data store, data flow, or trust boundary. List misses in gaps.

prompts.title: Write the readable report
prompts.stop_condition: P-report is the sole author of report.markdown. The document is complete and reflects the final matrix, including SRF columns only when Track B ran. reviewer is null. chain_meta uses the pack root version.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Shostack question: Did we do a good job?
Step: P-report. Finalize the readable threat model after P-qa, or after P-srf-owner when Track B was selected. This is the only step that authors report.markdown. A reviewer must be able to read it without opening the rest of the object.

Full final matrix:
{{full_matrix}}

report.markdown sections, in this order:
1. Title and a metadata table: date, method (Shostack Four Questions; STRIDE on in-scope elements and crossing flows; PHANTOM-B on llm_subset), role, representation, perspective, pack version, and empty reviewer.
2. Claim boundary.
3. Attacker assumptions and positions.
4. Architecture, trust boundaries, in_scope, out_of_scope, and documented replica inheritance.
5. Existing controls with diagram referent, shown coverage, and coverage basis.
6. Control gaps observed in the diagram. Phrase each as not shown, with expected_referent. Do not claim deployed absence.
7. Immediate review order when review_order is present. Call it review order, not risk rank.
8. Threats grouped by diagram_referent. Each: id, scenario, attacker_position, evidence_refs, STRIDE / PHANTOM-B / CIA, action, validation. Add Layer, Persona, and Party only when Track B fields are present.
9. Method coverage: STRIDE coverage counts; PHANTOM-B complete, incomplete, or not applicable. When llm_subset_empty is true, say PHANTOM-B was not applicable, never complete.
10. What this model does not claim.
11. qa.gaps and open_assumptions.
12. Reviewer line with empty name and date fields.

Do not add or drop threats. Set qa.report_present true.
Set chain_meta.method to the method sentence above, chain_meta.date to an ISO date, chain_meta.prompt_pack_version to {{pack_version}}, chain_meta.reviewer to null, and chain_meta.track_b_applied true only when every threat has srf.persona and srf.party.

prompts.title: Join AI Exchange slugs
prompts.stop_condition: When a threat matches a published AI Exchange slug in threats.json, copy layer, affected_layers, persona, and party for the named operating model. Do not re-derive those rows.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Track B is optional. Off by default. This step assigns SRF accountability. It does not invent threats.

Step: P-srf-join. Fetch https://aisharedresponsibility.com/data/threats.json now. Use only ids that exist in that file.

Published AI Exchange slugs: directpromptinjection, indirectpromptinjection, evasion, runtimemodelpoison, devmodelpoison, datapoison, supplymodelpoison, disclosureinoutput, modelinversionandmembership, devdataleak, modelexfiltration, runtimemodelleak, devmodelleak, airesourceexhaustion, inputdataleak, outputcontainsconventionalinjection.

threats.json also contains DSGAI-keyed ids (dsgai02, dsgai03, dsgai05, dsgai06, dsgai09, dsgai10, dsgai11, dsgai12, dsgai13, dsgai14, dsgai15, dsgai16, dsgai17, dsgai19, dsgai21). Those are not AI Exchange slugs. Do not put a dsgai id in srf.join.ai_exchange_slug.

Operating model: {{operating_model}}
Full Track A matrix:
{{full_matrix}}

For each threat, if the scenario is the same failure as a slug, set:

  srf.join.copied_from_threats_json = true

prompts.stop_condition: Every threat has srf.layer in L1-L5. Joined rows keep the copied layer.

prompts.stop_condition: Every threat has exactly one srf.persona from personas.json and one srf.party of customer or provider. Shared is not a final answer.

{{shared_rules}}

Track B. Step: P-srf-owner. Name one accountable persona and one party per threat, then return the entire matrix for P-report.

Fetch now:
- https://aisharedresponsibility.com/data/personas.json
- https://aisharedresponsibility.com/data/matrix.json

Persona ids (cosai-core only unless the diagram is a federated consortium): agentic-platform-provider, application-developer, data-provider, ai-system-users, ai-system-governance, model-provider, ai-model-serving, ai-platform-provider.

Full matrix with joined/layered threats:
{{full_matrix}}

prompts.title: Write the downloadable markdown report
prompts.stop_condition: The assistant reply equals report.markdown from the completed matrix, with no regeneration, JSON wrapper, fence, or commentary.

prompts.title: Write the completed JSON file
prompts.stop_condition: The assistant reply is the complete schema-valid matrix as pretty-printed JSON. report.markdown is preserved byte for byte, report.reviewer is null, and chain_meta.prompt_pack_version equals the pack root version.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

Step: P-export-json. Write the completed threat-model JSON file. Output JSON only. Pretty-print with two-space indent. No fences and no commentary outside the object.

Completed matrix:
{{full_matrix}}

This is a serialization step, not an authoring step:
- Keep every field and value already present. Do not add, drop, or rewrite threats.
- Preserve report.markdown byte for byte. If it is missing, stop and run P-report.
- Require qa.report_present true, report.reviewer null, and chain_meta.reviewer null.
- Require chain_meta.prompt_pack_version to equal {{pack_version}}.
- Require llm_subset_empty and nullable qa.phantom_b_complete to agree with the matrix.
- Require stride_coverage.complete true.
- Every mitigate or eliminate action.control_point must be a component, store, flow, or trust-boundary id and must have validation.
- srf.party is never shared.

Return the complete matrix, pretty-printed with two-space indentation.

prompts.title: Write the threat-database CSV
prompts.stop_condition: The assistant reply is RFC 4180 CSV with a header and one row per threat. No fences.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

This step writes the threat database. Output CSV only, starting at the header row. Do not wrap it in a JSON object or in fences.

Step: P-export-csv. Consume the completed matrix after P-report. Flatten threats[] into a spreadsheet a tracker or GRC tool can import.

Full matrix:
{{full_matrix}}

The header is intentionally stable across Track A and Track B so one GRC import mapping works for both. Track A leaves SRF cells empty rather than removing the columns.

Header, exactly these columns in this order:
system_name,threat_id,review_position,scenario,diagram_referent,attacker_position,preconditions,evidence_refs,asset,source,stride,phantom_b,cia,action_type,action_detail,control_point,validation_kind,validation_detail,owasp_llm_top10,ai_exchange_slug,atlas,srf_layer,srf_persona,srf_party,srf_note

Row rules:
- One row per threat. Include every threat. Do not add threats.
- threat_id is threats[].id. review_position comes from review_order when present and is empty otherwise.
- evidence_refs is the ids joined with a pipe, no spaces.
- system_name is the matrix system_name on every row.
- stride, phantom_b, and cia are the letters joined with a pipe, no spaces. Empty array is an empty cell.
- action_type, action_detail, and control_point come from action.
- validation_kind and validation_detail come from action.validation. Empty when validation is null.
- owasp_llm_top10, ai_exchange_slug, and atlas come from citations, or from srf.join.ai_exchange_slug when citations.ai_exchange_slug is empty.
- srf_layer, srf_persona, srf_party, and srf_note come from srf when present. Leave all four cells empty when Track B was not run. srf.party is never shared.
- Use RFC 4180: UTF-8, comma separators, wrap a field in double quotes when it contains a comma, quote, or newline, and escape a quote as two quotes.
- Write an empty cell for a missing value. Do not write null.
- Do not invent ids, slugs, or personas.

prompts.title: Write the Mermaid threat-model diagram
prompts.stop_condition: The assistant reply is Mermaid flowchart source that uses only inventory ids. Every threat id appears on its diagram_referent. No invented nodes. No fences.
prompts.template:
{{shared_rules}}

This step writes the Mermaid threat-model diagram. Output Mermaid flowchart source only, starting at the first %% line or the flowchart keyword. Do not wrap it in a JSON object or in markdown fences.

Step: P-export-diagram. Consume the completed matrix after P-report. Draw the inventory as a data-flow diagram and hang each threat id on the referent it already names. This diagram does not replace the uploaded source representation.

Full matrix:
{{full_matrix}}

Required shape:
1. First line: %% Threat model: {system_name}
2. Second line: flowchart LR (use TB only if LR will not fit).
3. One subgraph per inventory.trust_boundaries row. The subgraph id is that boundary id. Its contains[] members are the only nodes inside it.
4. One node per inventory component, external_actor, and data_store. Mermaid node id is the inventory id with hyphens changed to underscores. The visible label is inventory.name, then a line break, then every threat id whose diagram_referent equals that inventory id, joined by spaces.
5. Data stores use the cylinder shape: id[("name")].
6. One edge per inventory.data_flows row: from -->|label| to. If a threat names that flow id as diagram_referent, append those threat ids to the edge label.
7. classDef llm for llm_subset nodes. classDef drawnControl for every existing_controls[].coverage_referents id. Use diagram_referent only when coverage_referents is empty. Do not add control nodes.
8. If inventory.missing_trust_boundaries is true, write %% missing_trust_boundaries: true and draw no subgraphs.
9. Add %% replica_coverage lines for inherited pairs. Do not merge or omit replica nodes.
10. After the flowchart, a %% legend listing each threat id, its diagram_referent, stride letters, action.type, and review position when present. One threat per line.

Rules:
- Use only ids that exist in the inventory. Do not invent components, actors, stores, flows, vendors, or trust boundaries.
- Include every inventory node and every data_flow.
- Include every threat id exactly once on its referent (node, edge, or boundary annotation).
- Do not add nodes for attackers, threats, actions, or control absences.
- Do not draw an attack tree.
- Do not put proposed mitigations on the graph. drawnControl marks only controls already shown in the source diagram.
- If a referent is missing from inventory, omit that annotation and add %% gap: threat {id} referent {referent} not in inventory.
